L2t: Adhesive wound closure strips (such as Steri-Strips) are thin sterile tapes used to hold wound edges together after suturing or in minor lacerations.
L3t: Adhesive strips are designed to loosen and curl at the edges on their own over several days, and this gradual lifting is a normal part of healing that needs no clinical instrument or skilled procedure.
L4t: Removal of adhesive strips is simple enough that the patient can do it themselves at home, without needing a clinician.
L2f: Adhesive wound closure strips are thick rubberised bands that are stitched into the skin edges and usually remain in place for several weeks.
L3f: Adhesive strips bond so firmly to healing tissue that taking them off earlier than a full week risks reopening the wound, so a set minimum waiting period must pass before any removal.
L4f: Removal of adhesive strips should not be undertaken until at least seven days after application.
